text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A team of 38 foreign observers arrive from the United States to monitor Nigeria's local council election on Saturday.
- Nigeria's naira currency now 85 to $1 from 80 previously; central bank decision.
- Oil minister Dan Etete warns management of Nigerian liquefied natural gas company not to toy with the project which he says is a priority for the government.
- Lagos port container terminal staff back to work after one day strike over service conditions.
- Exiled leaders of opposition NADECO group and many others charged to court for treason for allegedly waging war against Nigeria through recent spate of bomb blasts in the country.
- Police deploy officers nationwide to ensure successful conduct of local council election on Saturday.
- Lagos state says it may seal off premises of about 2,000 firms that have not paid tax worth seven billion naira.
- Security forces foil attempt by some persons to steal kerosene from a broken fuel pipeline in Epe area of Lagos state.
- The 20 billion naira Bonny oil export terminal will soon be ready, says the project leader Stephen Owedimo.
- Nigeria is the future market in Africa in terms of foreign investment and international trade, Brazilian ambassador Geraldo Muzzi tells a seminar in Lagos.
- Cashew farmers seek government support to encourage export.
- Benue Cement Company share price slumps by five percent on the stock exchange.
